conclusion.title: BatchEnsemble: An alternative approach to Efficient Ensemble and Lifelong Learning
conclusion.read_kind: Reused frozen Round13 paper conclusions/text custody; targeted revisit for evaluation batching/complete-member work question, not another full-paper read
conclusion.exact_read_scope: Retained HTML text LF427–582: Section3.1 vectorization and test input repetition; Section3.2 hardware utilization/storage; rank-one/fixed-first-task limits. This packet binds B1/B2 exact slices427–568. Prior full focused assessment remains in round13_neural_enkf_qualification_v1.
conclusion.method_implementation_takeaway: Rank-one ensemble weights equal input/output feature scaling. Test evaluation repeats each input for all members in one effective M*B batch. Speed depends on hardware utilization; sharing W does not remove complete per-member dense transforms.
conclusion.GNNM_implication: Attribute boundary BE vectorization to BatchEnsemble; batch private GNNM trajectories through common maps with a leading member dimension, preserving all four outputs. This supports an implementation extension and useful broader GNNM work, without requiring a wholly new batching primitive.
conclusion.limitations_next_decision: Existing paper timings do not qualify selected GNNM checkpoints/graphs. Keep all member work and modern competent untied/head baselines; require whole trained-checkpoint serving utility and unchanged conformal results.

conclusion.verified_title: HG-Adapter: Improving Pre-Trained Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks with Dual Adapters
conclusion.publication_status: arXiv v1; later venue not verified in this bounded lane
exact_read_scope: Sections2.1-2.4: typed graph definition, dual low-rank structure adapters, relation weights, label propagation and objectives; theorem statements read, proofs not audited
AppendixB algorithm; adjacent proof beginning was visible, no proof audit
AppendixD.3-D.5 downstream protocol, architecture and computing-resource claims
paper_evidence: Section2.3 Eq4 factorizes adapter W_delta=W_down W_up before ReLU; W_vartheta for same-type structure similarity is also decomposed into low-rank matrices.
Same-type homogeneous structure is a positive symmetrized k-nearest-neighbor similarity graph; adapter output A F is added to frozen post-message embeddings.
Section2.3 Eq8-10 uses another low-rank adapter and a per-target-node softmax across neighbor/relation types; its weighted neighbor representation is added to frozen heterogeneous embeddings.
Section2.4 uses training-label propagation A Y, class-subgraph contrast, feature reconstruction and a margin objective. AppendixD.3 evaluates probabilities from similarity to class-subgraph vectors.
Algorithm initializes/uploads pretraining, then tunes adapters/projection. Exact factor initialization, k, rank and initial learning-rate value are not fixed by the selected implementation paragraph.
conclusion.saved_takeaway: Low-rank graph adaptation with typed structural weighting and label-informed optimization is direct prior. It is not a BatchEnsemble committee or proof of an exact node/relation-indexed rank-one ensemble.
conclusion.candidate_relationship: Defeats novelty based on adding heterogeneity, compact adapters, task-related relation weighting or supervised graph structure alone. It adds member-specific structural propagation work if turned into an ensemble.
limitations: No author-linked implementation URL found in the retained paper HTML; exact implementation not retrieved.
The generalization theorem statements were read for method context; their proof, pseudo-label-as-extra-sample assumptions and graph-dependence conditions were not independently validated.

conclusion.verified_title: CHoE: Cross-Domain Heterogeneous Graph Prompt Learning via Structure-Conditioned Experts

exact_read_scope.scope_note: Method and heterograph definitions fully scoped; no claim of all paper/references read.

conclusion.saved_takeaway: Frozen per-meta-path self-supervised HAN/GAT experts are routed using positive/negative edge similarity, temperature and cumulative load penalty; downstream prompts fuse meta-path semantics. Genuine node/relation types are modeled. Code verifies1024edge-pair samples, no-gradient routing score, per-meta-path/global rather than per-node expert weights, cumulative loads updated in training, and prompts/classifier as optimizer parameters.
conclusion.relationship_to_GNNM_and_extension: Shows heterogeneous graph-view specialization, structural gating and load balancing are prior. Structure similarity can fail to reflect class-error complementarity.
conclusion.attributed_prior_vs_open_gap: Attribute pretrained relation/meta-path experts, edge-similarity routing and anti-collapse load penalties. Open utility gap is training-label predictive complementarity in parameter-shared graph routes, without extra self-supervised pretraining or inference gate.
conclusion.decisive_next_step: Routing source resolved. Do not label its scalar meta-path expert routing per-node or class-conditional; heterograph class complementarity remains an empirical question.

conclusion.title: Relation-Aware Graph Foundation Model
conclusion.takeaway: REEF conditions aggregator/classifier generators on relation tokens, and dataset projector/bias on dataset descriptions. Its v2 heterograph extension uses typed projections and canonical relations on original HGB ACM/DBLP splits; its complete recipe includes text encoders/SVD/augmentation/multi-dataset pretraining. Exact interrelation generator tying is unclear from relation-indexed notation without code.
conclusion.candidate_difference: One supervised CP-factorized member×canonical-relation output scaling on shared native HGT message cores, without REEF generator/pretraining/text pipeline. Conditional parameter generation is attributed; complete-method equality not claimed.
conclusion.remaining_qualification: No author code/source/pretraining/native HGB reproduction; source performance paragraph incidental and ignored.

conclusion.title: Empowering Heterogeneous Graph Foundation Models via Decoupled Relation Alignment
conclusion.takeaway: DRSA shares fixed random low-rank endpoint-type bilinear operators across relations, estimates structure-driven representations and decomposes semantics/residuals before a shared pretraining encoder. Printed M_r=A_source B_target^T gives the same operator for same endpoint types.
conclusion.candidate_difference: Canonical-relation private diagonal tensor interaction during supervised recurrent HGT, rather than multi-domain preprocessing/latent reconstruction. Typed low-rank sharing itself is prior.
conclusion.remaining_qualification: Convergence/source assumptions/implementation not independently audited; no native few-shot transfer or cost reproduction.
